title: Orphaned future-work direction from W4386564359 (2016)
explanation: Future-work item from openalex:W4386564359 (2016) is unaddressed by any later corpus paper through 2026 (10 yrs). 37 later topically-near papers exist and none addresses it (two-stage matcher). Item: "Determining whether a polynomial-time algorithm exists to find a fair assignment of minimum loss or decide existence of a non-trivial fair assignment ". CORPUS-RELATIVE CAVEAT: 'orphaned' means unaddressed WITHIN this 101-paper corpus, not the field; the two-stage matcher's precision is limited (P≈0.64) and the corpus is a sample, so this is a weak, corpus-relative signal — not evidence the field ignored it.

caveats.label: Corpus-relative

consumer.headline: Determining whether a polynomial-time algorithm exists to find a fair assignment of minimum loss or decide existence of a non-trivial fair assignment when feature vectors can be split across multiple bins.
consumer.kind_short: A question a paper said needed studying, that nothing else in this library followed up on
consumer.kind_long: When researchers finish a paper they usually name the questions they could not get to. We collected those, then checked whether any later paper in this library actually went and did the work. These are the ones where nothing did.
consumer.strength_meaning: There is real evidence behind this, but it rests on a small number of papers — read them before trusting it.
consumer.why: A paper said this needed studying. That was 10 years ago. Since then 37 later papers in this library worked on closely related topics, and none of them took this up.

caveats.label: Only checked within these 101 papers
caveats.text: Nothing in this library followed this up — but this library is 101 papers, not the whole field. Somebody outside it may well have answered this already. Check before you invest.

caveats.label: Based partly on summaries only
caveats.text: For some of these papers we only had the summary, not the full text. Papers we could read in full reveal far more about their own limits, so this may be built on an incomplete picture.
